text.p: Following are the main stories in Slovenia's Friday morning newspapers.
- Government raises petrol prices by 9.5 percent.
- Organisers of the final ski-jumping World Cup competition in Planica, Slovenia, said the match would take place despite a lack of snow.
- The Ljubljana city council rejected a proposal of the capital's 1997 budget, claiming it was not detailed enough.
- The Christian Democratic Party proposed a merger with the conservative People's Party 10 times in the past couple of years, all of which the People's Party has rejected.
- Association of Employers said negotiations with unions on work benefits were progressing and should be finished as scheduled by the end of May.
- The Maribor city council said it would start a court case against mayor Alojz Krizman, claiming Krizman illegally raised his own salary and salaries of four deputies.
- Foreign Minister Zoran Thaler said Slovenia's main goal was full membership in the European Union.
- Shares of investment funds that participated in Slovenia's massive privatisation process are expected to be listed on the over-the-counter (OTC) market of the Ljubljana bourse in autumn.
- The government proposed a freeze of managers' salaries, which rose 24 percent in 1996 and represent 11 percent of all salaries.
